hypothesis: Replacing the ReactiveSession-per-call pattern in Neo4jGraphSuspendOperations with blocking session + withContext(Dispatchers.IO) for single-value ops should reduce avg_latency_us by 20-35% because the reactive->flow->list pipeline adds mutex, Channel, and allocation overhead with no benefit for these ops.

steps.change: Promote the existing `syncDelegate` lazy property (currently only used by algorithm methods at lines 354-386) to be the primary delegate for all single-value suspend ops. Keep its lazy initialization pattern: `private val syncDelegate by lazy { Neo4jGraphOperations(driver, database) }`. This eliminates the need for ReactiveSession in single-value paths while still sharing the same Driver.

Rewrite `runQuery` helper (lines 82-96) to a blocking-IO variant: `private suspend fun <T> runQueryIo(cypher: String, params: Map<String, Any?> = emptyMap(), mapper: (Record) -> T): List<T> = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) { driver.session(SessionConfig.builder().withDatabase(database).build()).use { s -> s.run(cypher, params).list(mapper) } }`. Keep the old reactive `runQuery` for any callers that truly need streaming, OR rename the blocking version and remove the reactive one if unused after step 3-5.

Convert all single-value suspend ops to delegate to syncDelegate + withContext(Dispatchers.IO), matching the algorithm pattern at lines 354-386. Specifically rewrite: `createVertex` (lines 152-162), `findVertexById` (lines 164-173), `updateVertex` (lines 189-200), `deleteVertex` (lines 202-216), `countVertices` (lines 218-229), `createEdge` (lines 233-254), `deleteEdge` (lines 270-283), `shortestPath` (lines 310-329), `dropGraph` (lines 128-131), `graphExists` (lines 133-145). Each becomes e.g. `override suspend fun findVertexById(label: String, id: GraphElementId): GraphVertex? = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) { syncDelegate.findVertexById(label, id) }`. This removes ReactiveSession allocation, Publisher->Flow conversion, asFlow/toList Channel overhead, and awaitSingle/awaitFirstOrNull continuation hops per call.

Keep Flow-returning ops (`findVerticesByLabel`, `findEdgesByLabel`, `neighbors`, `allPaths`) using the existing `flowQuery` reactive helper, since streaming benefits from ReactiveSession backpressure. Do NOT change these methods. This preserves reactive semantics where they actually matter.

Remove now-unused imports if the reactive `runQuery` helper is fully removed: `kotlinx.coroutines.NonCancellable`, `kotlinx.coroutines.reactive.asFlow`, `kotlinx.coroutines.reactive.awaitFirstOrNull`, `kotlinx.coroutines.reactive.awaitSingle`, `kotlinx.coroutines.flow.toList`, and remove the private `session()` factory + reactive `runQuery` if only `flowQuery` still uses `session()`. Keep the session() helper if flowQuery still uses it. Update the class KDoc (lines 42-65) to note that single-value ops use blocking+IO delegation while Flow ops use ReactiveSession streaming.

Verify coroutine semantics: (a) `withContext(Dispatchers.IO)` preserves structured concurrency and cancellation propagation (unlike the current `NonCancellable`-wrapped close). (b) Blocking JDBC Driver session is safe on Dispatchers.IO (documented intended use). (c) No behavioral change for callers: return types (GraphVertex/GraphEdge/Boolean/Long/GraphPath?) remain identical. Run `./gradlew :graph-neo4j:test` to confirm existing Neo4jGraphSuspendOperationsTest passes unchanged.

expected_outcome.rationale: Current per-call cost includes: (1) ReactiveSession allocation via reflective session(class, config), (2) Publisher<ReactiveResult> -> awaitSingle continuation, (3) Publisher<Record> -> Flow via asFlow (Channel allocation + mutex), (4) Flow.toList collection, (5) NonCancellable withContext for close + awaitFirstOrNull. Replacing with syncDelegate + withContext(Dispatchers.IO) collapses this to: (1) blocking Session via session().use, (2) direct Result.list(mapper), (3) one Dispatchers.IO context switch. Removes ~4 allocation sites and 2-3 continuation hops per call. The algorithm methods already prove this pattern works (lines 354-386) - this hypothesis extends it to CRUD paths.

sub_score_expectations.allocation_rate: significant reduction (no Channel, no Flow builder)
sub_score_expectations.context_switches: reduced from 3-4 per call to 1 per call

evidence_verified.precedent_confirmed: syncDelegate lazy pattern + withContext(Dispatchers.IO) already used for pageRank/degreeCentrality/connectedComponents/bfs/dfs/detectCycles at lines 354-386.

(5) Implementation clarity PASS - every method listed with before/after pattern. (6) Expected outcome PASS - 20-35% is plausible given removal of 4 allocations + 2-3 continuation hops per call.
structural_concerns: Minor: step 6 notes `withContext(Dispatchers.IO)` restores cancellation semantics that the current NonCancellable close pattern breaks - this is a subtle behavior change. Callers that rely on close-on-cancel-suppression could see different lifecycle behavior, but the plan states return types are unchanged and existing tests must pass, which gates this risk.

Minor: step 2 describes both `runQueryIo` AND potentially renaming/removing the reactive runQuery - executor should pick one path. Recommend: introduce `runQueryIo` then remove reactive `runQuery` in step 5 cleanup once Flow ops are confirmed to only use `flowQuery`.
